title: headless-home-server config
description: Identifiers and choices only. Secrets (tunnel credentials, API keys, passwords) never go in this file.

adminUser.description: The macOS admin account you log in with. Deploys run as this user.

serviceUser.description: Hidden non-admin account that runs every service and the tunnel.

lanIp.description: The server's LAN address, for the SSH alias. Reserve it on your router.

repoPath.description: Where your clone lives on the server, e.g. ~/git/my-home-server.

exposure.description: Needed only when a service uses auth public or access.

accessTeam.description: Cloudflare Zero Trust team name, for services with auth access.

dir.description: Folder that holds the service, in this repo or, with source, in that repo. It is copied to the service user's home on deploy.

run.description: Command started inside that folder, as the service user. It gets PORT and HOST=127.0.0.1.

auth.description: public: anyone on the internet via the tunnel (the service does its own auth). access: via the tunnel, behind a Cloudflare Access policy. gateway: an MCP server behind the OAuth gateway (needs an mcp block). tailscale: only your tailnet. local: only this machine (reach it over SSH).

hostname.description: Public hostname, for public and access.

accessAud.description: Application Audience tag of the Access app, for access.

user.description: own: the service runs as its own hidden user (<serviceUser>_<name>) with its own home, secrets and data. shared: it runs as serviceUser, like the tunnel.

mcp.description: Publish this service as an MCP namespace through the gateway, at https://<gateway.hostname>/<name>. Needs expose.auth gateway.

tools.description: The only tools the gateway lists and lets through. Anything else the server offers stays hidden.

clients.description: Who may use it: oauth:claude (Claude's apps), oauth:chatgpt, bearer:<name>. Nobody else.

source.description: Take the service's code from another git repo instead of this one. dir is then a folder in that repo ('.' for its root). To ship a new version, change rev and deploy.

repo.description: Git URL the admin user can fetch, e.g. git@github.com:you/app.git with a read-only deploy key.

rev.description: The full commit hash to deploy. A pin, never a branch, so this repo's history records every version that ran.

jobs.description: Commands that run on a schedule as the service's user, in its folder, with its secrets and data. Each is a LaunchDaemon <prefix>.<service>.<job>; its log is <service>.<job>.log.

run.description: Command started in the service's folder.

at.description: Times of day, HH:MM, in the server's time zone.

runAtLoad.description: Also run at boot and after each deploy. launchd catches up on a time missed during sleep, but not one missed while the Mac was off; this covers that.

gateway.description: The OAuth gateway (a Cloudflare Worker in gateway/) that puts every service with an mcp block at https://<hostname>/<service name>, for claude.ai, ChatGPT and bearer-token clients. docs/gateway.md.

hostname.description: Where AI apps connect, e.g. mcp.example.com. The Worker gets it as a custom domain.

originHostname.description: The tunnel hostname only the gateway uses, e.g. origin.example.com. Each MCP service is at /<name>/ on it, behind Access.

originAccessAud.description: Audience tag of the Access app for originHostname, whose policy allows only the gateway's service token.

kvNamespaceId.description: KV namespace for OAuth state: npx wrangler kv namespace create OAUTH_KV

allowedGithubId.description: The one GitHub account (numeric id) allowed to sign in.

usageDatabase.description: D1 database name for the usage log and health history (created on first deploy), or false for none.

statusHidden.description: Namespaces to leave off the public status page (GET /stats/history), e.g. an older URL for the same server.

publicFeedTools.description: Tools whose calls the public GET /stats/recent feed may show (app family, tool name, minute, latency, ok). Empty by default, which keeps the feed empty. List only tools whose names say nothing private.

statusPageUrl.description: Optional: your public status page (it reads /stats/history and turns on /alerts). The alerts page links back to it.

usageDatabaseId.description: Optional: the id of an existing D1 database to use for the usage log, so the deploy binds it instead of looking it up by name.

bearerClients.description: Clients that use a static token instead of OAuth (Claude Code, Codex, scripts): { name: sha256 hex of the token }. List them as bearer:<name> in a service's mcp.clients.

extraNamespaces.description: Advanced: namespaces that aren't services, e.g. an older URL kept working during a migration. { name: { path, origin, tools, clients } }
